This is a well-documented, biochemically and genetically consistent case of classical congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency (21-OHD) in a 46,XX individual. The diagnosis rests on the triad of: (1) unequivocal genetic female sex (46,XX karyotype), excluding gonadal or sex chromosome DSD; (2) markedly elevated basal 17-OHP — the hallmark biochemical signature of 21-OHD, with level >100 ng/dL being highly specific for classical disease; and (3) clinical and biochemical evidence of prenatal and postnatal androgen excess (clitoromegaly, labial fusion, hirsutism, acne, primary amenorrhea, elevated testosterone and DHEA-S) without mineralocorticoid deficiency (normal aldosterone, borderline-normal renin, no salt-wasting history). The preserved morning cortisol does not contradict the diagnosis — it reflects compensatory HPA axis activation and precursor shunting, a known feature of classical 21-OHD with intact glucocorticoid synthesis capacity *under stress*, but inadequate regulation. Low bone mass (Z-score −2.4) is a downstream consequence of chronic hyperandrogenemia, estrogen deficiency (due to anovulation/amenorrhea), and likely suboptimal glucocorticoid replacement — all aligning with long-standing undertreated disease. No contradictory findings are present (e.g., no evidence of 11β-hydroxylase deficiency — normal blood pressure, no hypokalemia; no 3β-HSD deficiency — no elevated DHEA or pregnenolone; no P450 oxidoreductase defect — no skeletal malformations or disordered steroidogenesis pattern). - Karyotype is 46,XX — confirms genetic female sex and excludes sex chromosome DSD.  
- Basal 17-hydroxyprogesterone is 145 ng/dL — >100 ng/dL, highly specific for classical 21-hydroxylase deficiency.  
- Total testosterone is 245 ng/dL — markedly elevated above normal female range (8–60 ng/dL).  
- DHEA-S is 320 μg/dL — elevated above typical premenopausal female upper limit (~220–250 μg/dL).

- Aldosterone is 8.2 ng/dL and renin is 1.8 ng/mL/hr — no biochemical evidence of mineralocorticoid deficiency or salt-wasting.
